title: Praying for the dead, again
hookLine: the communion between living and dead isn't broken
tomorrow: if the body is buried, why does the Creed end with it?

lines: CAN YOU STILL PRAY FOR HIM?
cards: A friend's grandpa dies. His family isn't religious. Can you still pray for him?
An old story asks nearly the same question. A battle is over. The next day Judas Maccabeus and his men go out to carry home their dead.
Under the coats of the fallen they find small charms from the idols of Jamnia, things their law forbade. These men died holding exactly what they shouldn't have. So what does Judas do?

teach.b: He doesn't write them off. Second Maccabees says Judas and his men turned to prayer, asking that the sin be blotted out.
Then they took up a collection and sent it to Jerusalem for a sacrifice for the dead, because, the writer says, they hoped the dead would rise.
His verdict, in the Douay-Rheims: "It is therefore a holy and wholesome thought to pray for the dead." Notice who they prayed for. Not heroes.
Men who died with the wrong thing in their pockets.
Paul gives the reason this works: "whether we live, or whether we die, we are the Lord's." Death moves someone, but not out of God's hands, so it doesn't cut the line between us.
The Church calls that line the communion of saints: the living, the dead being made ready for God, and the saints in heaven, still one family.
A preface said at Masses for the dead puts it in four Latin words: vita mutatur, non tollitur.

teach.h: LIFE IS CHANGED, NOT TAKEN AWAY.
teach.b: Life is changed, not taken away.
One to tell a friend: one of the Mass's Eucharistic Prayers remembers all the dead whose faith God alone has known. It doesn't check anyone's paperwork first.
That's why the Church still prays for the dead at every Mass, by name when it can, and leaves the judging to God.

how: Catholics pray for the dead at every Mass, have Masses offered for them, and pray the Eternal Rest prayer, especially in November and on the anniversary of a death.

games.q: what does “praying for the dead” mean?
o: a rite only priests do at a funeral Mass
asking God's mercy for people who have died
asking the dead to grant you favors or luck

games.q: who's on the battlefield — tap the pairs.
p: prayed for soldiers who died wrong
found under the fallen soldiers' coats
life is changed, not taken away
whether we live or die, we are the Lord's

s: Catholics only pray for the dead who were good Catholics
Judas prayed for men who died holding idols' charms, and a Mass prayer remembers all the dead whose faith God alone knows.
praying for the dead has roots in the Bible
Second Maccabees calls it a holy and wholesome thought.
once someone dies, the bond with the living is cut
the communion of saints: the living and the dead, still one family in God.

games.q: your teammate's grandpa died. he never went to church, and she says praying for him would be "fake." what fits Judas's battlefield?
o: offer to pray for him quietly, and just be with her.
agree; prayer for the dead is only for believers.
tell her he's surely fine, so prayer isn't needed.
games.why: Judas prayed for men who died with the wrong thing in their pockets. Catholics pray for the dead without checking credentials, and leave the judging to God.

practice: Say one name out loud, someone who has died: family, a friend, a friend's grandparent you barely knew. Hold the name for a few breaths, as if it were still a conversation.
If you pray, the old words are these: eternal rest grant unto them, O Lord, and let perpetual light shine upon them.

wordCard.voice: Praying for the dead. Love spoken as prayer for those who have died, because death doesn't cut the line.

orig.note: Latin: life is changed, not taken away. from a preface said at Masses for the dead.

carryVoice: Your line: not broken. The dead are still family, and prayer still reaches them. See you tomorrow.
